key_insight: Dex-One2Many learns dexterous manipulation from just one human demonstration, but avoids overfitting to that single motion by using it as guidance rather than a strict template. This helps the policy generalize to new object poses, goals, and grasps.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of learning dexterous robot manipulation when only a single human video is available. Existing imitation methods often copy motions too rigidly, while RL alone is too hard to train from scratch in high-dimensional action spaces.
method: Use one human demonstration as weak prior guidance instead of exact motion matching.
Combine imitation-style initialization with reinforcement learning to discover better manipulation behaviors.
Aim for one-to-many generalization: one demo, many valid robot trajectories and grasps.
impact: This approach reduces the need for expensive robot demonstrations and makes dexterous manipulation learning more practical. For practitioners, it offers a path to train more adaptable manipulation policies from very limited demonstration data.

paper_title: Dex-One2Many: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Human Demonstration
paper_authors: Jusuk Lee, Sungha Kim, Yeonsoo Park, Jonguk Cheon, Yoonkyo Jung
